title: APT-CGLP: Advanced Persistent Threat Hunting via Contrastive Graph-Language Pre-Training

problem.claim: Provenance-based threat hunting aims to identify Advanced Persistent Threats on endpoints by correlating CTI attack patterns with provenance graphs derived from system audit logs.

gap.claim: The graph-matching pipeline loses substantial information during graph extraction and requires intensive manual curation, limiting scalability and effectiveness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Provenance-based threat hunting correlates CTI attack patterns with provenance graphs from system audit logs to identify endpoint APTs.
The central challenge is the structural and semantic modality gap between provenance graphs and CTI reports.
Prior work treats threat hunting as graph matching by extracting attack graphs from CTI reports and aligning them with provenance graphs.
This prior pipeline suffers information loss during graph extraction and depends heavily on manual curation, undermining scalability and effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: A threat-hunting workflow must connect structurally different provenance graphs and CTI reports.

interpretation.claim: Representational alignment is a central design concern when combining graph-structured telemetry with textual intelligence.

application.claim: Applications involving heterogeneous graph and text evidence may benefit from methods that reduce modality mismatch before matching or retrieval.

exception.claim: The supplied units do not establish that reducing modality mismatch improves detection or generalizes beyond this threat-hunting setting.

unknowns: The abstract units do not describe the proposed method or its implementation.
No experimental setup, datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results are supplied.
No explicit author-stated novelty claim is supplied.
